etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Derived from Middle French oblique, borrowed from Latin obliqūus.
senses: Not parallel or perpendicular to the base.
Not straightforward; indirect; by implication; (sometimes even) obscure, ambiguous, or confusing.
(typography) Synonym of slash: the typographic mark ⟨/⟩.
(intransitive) To deviate from a perpendicular line; to become askew.
(military) To march in a direction oblique to the line of the column or platoon; — formerly accomplished by oblique steps, now by direct steps, the men half-facing either to the right or left.
